stem: What was the impact of railways on Indian industries during the colonial period?

options.label: a
options.text: Hindered industrial development by promoting imports.

options.label: b
options.text: Entrepreneurship was encouraged in remote areas.

options.label: c
options.text: Promoted industrial development by providing cheap transport.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The first railway in India ran in 1853 between Bombay and Thane. During the colonial period, the development of railways promoted imports and created obstacles to industrial development. As a result, it had a negative impact on Indian industries.

In 1793, Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement system of land revenue. It was also known by different names such as Istemrari, Jagirdari, Malguzari and Biswedari, etc. This system was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha and Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. Under it, about 19% of the total area of British India was covered. Under this arrangement, a new class of zamindars was declared as landowners. They had to pay 10/11 of the land revenue to the Company and could keep 1/11 for their services.

stem: The Ryotwari system was first implemented in –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Ryotwari system was first introduced experimentally in the Madras Presidency by Alexander Read in 1792 in the Baramahal region of Tamil Nadu. Thomas Munro is closely associated with the Ryotwari system. After becoming the Governor of Madras in 1820, he implemented it throughout the Madras Presidency. Munro’s disciple Elphinstone introduced it in the Bombay Presidency. This system was implemented in about 51% of the total area of British India (Madras, some parts of Bombay, Assam and Coorg now a part of modern Karnataka, etc.). Under this system, ryots were given ownership rights over land, and they were directly and individually responsible for paying land revenue. After 1835, G. Wingate and H. E. Goldsmith introduced reforms in this system.

stem: Who introduced the system of Mahalwari Settlement in Bengal?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In 1822, Holt Mackenzie prepared a new method of land-revenue administration, the Mahalwari system, in the Bengal Presidency of the North Western Province (most of this area lies in present-day Uttar Pradesh). In this system, nearly 30% of British India’s land area was included, along with the Central Provinces and Punjab. The Mahalwari system contained elements of both the Zamindari and Ryotwari systems. In the asked question, the word “Bengal” has been used, which is incorrect; instead, the term “Bengal Presidency” is more appropriate. Therefore, option (c) is correct. The Bihar Public Service Commission also considered option (c) as correct in both its original and revised answer keys.

stem: What was the name also given to the forced labor (begar) or illegal levy demanded from the farmer by the landlord?
expl: The begar (unpaid forced labour) or illegal levy demanded by zamindars from cultivators was called Vethi. The practice of making people work without wages is called begar; that is, it is a kind of unpaid forced labour.

stem: Home Charges or the expenses of the Indian government in Britain included:

options.label: b
options.text: Military and other stores purchased in India

expl: Home Charges, i.e., the expenditure of the Government of India in Britain, included the pensions of British officials serving in India, military and other stores purchased in England and supplied to India, and the guaranteed interest paid to railway investors. Here, due to an error in the option, it is written “military and other stores purchased in India,” whereas “purchased in England and supplied to India” is more accurate, as mentioned by historians like Bipan Chandra as well.

stem: In which year was the first cotton textile mill established in India?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The first cotton textile mill in India was established in 1818 at Fort Gloster near Kolkata. However, this mill proved to be a commercial failure and was shut down.
